title: Nocturne
audience: Fragrance buyers discovering a new evening scent
narrativeConcept: The name emerges from darkness the way light catches black glass: one word, then a promise, then the invitation.
creativeDirection: Near-black background with a disciplined gold accent. One centered line per shot, generous negative space, and the built-in glow and rings standing in for light on glass. Copy grows calmer and larger toward the end.

shots.purpose: Hook: introduce the name with nothing competing for attention.
shots.mainVisual: The name alone, centered, with the accent glow on the right.
shots.composition: Centered, large, a thin gold accent bar beneath at the lower left third.
shots.motionBehavior: The name rises in with a short glitch while the accent bar draws on, then holds.
shots.transitionIn: Opens on the brand background as the name fades up.
acceptanceCriteria: "Nocturne" is fully visible and legible from frame 18 to the end of the shot.

shots.purpose: Message: say what the scent is in one line.
shots.mainVisual: The line centered at full size.
shots.composition: Same centered system and accent placement as shot 1.
shots.motionBehavior: The line rises in with a short glitch, then holds long enough to read twice.
acceptanceCriteria: The whole line sits inside the safe area on every frame.

shots.purpose: Resolution: invite the viewer to act.
shots.mainVisual: The closing line centered, the accent bar fully drawn.
shots.composition: Centered, the largest type of the film.
shots.cameraBehavior: Locked off; holds through the final frame.
shots.motionBehavior: Fades up, then holds still to the last frame.
shots.transitionOut: Ends on a stable hold with no fade or blank frame.
acceptanceCriteria: "After dark" and the gold accent are visible on the last frame.

hardConstraints: Use the product name exactly as written: Nocturne.
Keep all copy inside the safe area.

technical: Total duration is 8.5 seconds, within one frame.
creative: Every line of copy has at least 4.5:1 contrast with the background.
The gold accent appears in every shot and nowhere else competes with the copy.
